Student pilots

10 gifts for teenagers interested in becoming pilots

A teenager’s aviation interest may lead toward flying, engineering, photography, simulation or history. A good gift leaves those paths open. These ideas help them explore without assuming they are ready for a particular training program or expensive equipment purchase.

By Pilot Gift Guide Updated 2026-10-20

How we choose our recommendations
In this guideThe ideasHow to chooseMore gift ideas

The ideas

Our selections prioritize personal relevance, usefulness, and fit for the recipient. Named products and destinations link to official sources where applicable.

  1. 1

    An aviation museum day

    Let the teenager help choose the collection. Include time to explore the exhibits that catch their attention rather than following a rigid checklist.

  2. 2

    A beginner-friendly aviation book

    Choose a readable introduction or engaging story. Dense professional manuals are rarely the best first step unless specifically requested.

  3. 3

    A flight simulator they can run

    Check the computer or console, edition and controls first. A compatible modest setup is better than unusable high-end hardware.

  4. 4

    A model-building project

    Match the complexity to their patience and experience. Consider the tools, supervision and display space the project requires.

  5. 5

    A local aviation event

    Use the organizer’s current information for dates, access and restrictions. Plan transport and any necessary adult supervision.

  6. 6

    A photography outing

    Explore a lawful public viewing location together. Existing camera equipment is enough to discover whether they enjoy the hobby.

  7. 7

    A notebook for aviation questions

    Encourage curiosity without turning it into homework. They can record aircraft, places and topics they want to investigate.

  8. 8

    A school-approved introductory experience

    Research providers with the family and confirm age, consent and booking terms. Let the teenager decide whether they want to participate.

  9. 9

    A book or kit about design and engineering

    This suits someone more interested in how aircraft work than in piloting. Choose a level that invites experimentation without unnecessary frustration.

  10. 10. Airport-radio listeners and plane spotters

    ATC — Live Air Traffic Radio

How to choose

Match the gift to their actual interest and involve a parent or guardian where appropriate. Check age restrictions and supervision requirements directly with activity providers. Avoid promising that a game, book or experience counts toward pilot training unless a qualified provider explicitly confirms it.

Prices and availability can change. Check the exact model, delivered total and return terms with the seller. Our recommendations are researched editorial selections, not hands-on test results.
